_comment: Fiat 500 L (1968) — engine 110F.000, and the car around it.
499.5 cc air-cooled OHV parallel twin, 67.4 x 70 mm, 7.1:1, 18 hp at
4600 rpm, one Weber 26 IMB carburettor for both cylinders.
The crank is a 360 degree one: both journals sit at the same angle, so the
pistons rise together and fire one full revolution apart. That even beat is
most of what makes a 500 sound like a 500, and it is not written down
anywhere below — it falls out of the journal angles and the firing order.
This is the same engine as the `fiat500` preset and as demo/fiat-500l.mr,
written as data instead. A test loads all three and checks they agree.
Units are SI: metres, cubic metres, radians, rad/s, newton metres,
kilograms. Keys starting with an underscore are comments.
name: Fiat 500 L (1968)
_preset: Any preset works as the starting point; the layout below replaces it.

layout._exhausts: Both pots into one small silencer, tucked in behind the engine.
layout._cylinders: Both journals at 0: a 360 degree crank.

_firingOrder: Two cylinders, one revolution apart: 0 and 360 degrees.

params._stroke: 70 mm, so the crank throw is half of it.
_carburettor: One 26 mm Weber for both cylinders. At 4600 rpm the engine wants about
40 CFM at 100% volumetric efficiency, and this is what stops it getting
there — the reason it makes 18 hp and runs out of breath at about
params._idleStop: Wound further open than a car engine's: a 500 idles near 800.
params._flywheel: Small, but the cast flywheel also drives the cooling fan.
params._revLimit: 5400 rpm. The carburettor is the real limit, not the limiter.

cam._comment: Mild pushrod cam: 200 degrees at 50 thou, 260 thou lift.

_comment: Small two-valve chamber with a ~28 mm inlet valve; the exhaust side
flows about three quarters of the inlet, as usual for a plain pushrod
head. Valve lift in metres against flow-bench SCFM at 28 inH2O.

_vehicleComment: The car. 499 kg, tall and slab-sided, on 125-12 tyres. The 4.875:1 final
drive and short ratios are why it revs so hard for so little speed.

vehicle._tireRadius: 125-12, so roughly a 10 inch rolling radius.
vehicle._clutch: A small single-plate clutch, comfortably above 18 hp worth of torque.

_gears: Four speeds, unsynchronised on first. Roughly 30, 47, 75 and 112 km/h at 4600 rpm.

audio._comment: Air-cooled and thin-panelled: mechanical edge, little damping.
